PP1 · Chapter 2 of 6

More, less and the same

Compare groups and everyday sizes without racing.

  1. See it
  2. Try it
  3. Practise it
  4. Print it
  5. Check it

This chapter works best after Count with me. You can still look around, or jump to the check.

By the end I can…

  • I can find more or fewer objects.
  • I can compare big, tall and thick things.
  • I can compare weight and how full a jar is.

1 See it

Screen 1 of 4

More or fewer?

Orange has 6. Blue has 3.

Orange has more.

Blue has fewer.

Screen 2 of 4

Tall, short, thick, thin

This tower is tall. This one is short.

This book is thick. This one is thin.

Screen 3 of 4

Heavy and light

The heavy side goes down.

The light side goes up.

When both are the same, the balance is level.

Screen 4 of 4

Full and empty

This jar is empty.

This jar is half full.

This jar is full.

Words to know
more
A bigger group. It has extra things.
fewer
A smaller group. It has less things.
same
Equal. Nothing is extra.
heavy
Hard to lift. The heavy side goes down.

Chapter passed. Next: Meet the shapes

For parents

What your child learns

Your child compares groups by matching one to one, and compares size, weight and how full things are. The words more, fewer, tall and heavy come first.

A common slip

Thinking the bigger-looking group has more. Line the objects up in two rows, one to one, so the extra ones show.

5-minute home activity: Bath-time compare

  1. Fill two cups, one full and one nearly empty.
  2. Ask, "Which is fuller? Which is empty?"
  3. Line up 4 toys and 2 toys. Ask which row has more.
  4. Pick two toys. Ask which one is heavier and why.
